newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ trade balance trend still improving - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ trade balance trend still improving - SNZ.

text.p: The trend estimate for New Zealand's trade balance continued to improve in July, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Monday.
It said the trade balance trend had been improving since a low point in February 1996.
"This is the result of the exports trend rising by an average of 1.4 percent per month, while the imports trend has remained virtually unchanged since February 1996," SNZ said.

In July, the unadjusted value of exports was NZ$1.82 billion, up 8.8 percent on June and 14.6 percent on July 1995. Major contributors to the rise were dairy produce, up $94 million, meat and edibile offal, up $37 million, and wool, up $21 million.
Exports that fell included wood pulp, down $19 million, and mineral fuels, down $11 million.
Unadjusted imports for the month of July 1996 were valued at NZ$1.94 billion, up 18.1 percent on June 1996 and 8.4 percent on the year ago figure.
Imports that rose included vehicles, up $80 million, and mechanical machinery, up $22 million. Fertilisers led the groups that recorded notable falls, down $37 million.
The trade balance recorded a deficit of NZ$122.5 million in July, compared with a surplus in June of $28.3 million and a deficit of $203.8 million for July 1995.

The trade balance for the year to July 1996 was $552 million in deficit, against a deficit of $402.1 million for the July 1995 year. Comparing these two years, exports rose by 0.1 percent to $20.95 billion, while imports were up 0.8 percent to $21.5 billion.
